why: deletes overriding method(s) renderStackForBone: whatever they did is gone -- port each to the new API, or say why vanilla no longer needs it; deletes overriding method(s) getStackForBone, getTransformTypeForStack, renderStackForBone: whatever they did is gone -- port each to the new API, or say why vanilla no longer needs it
reviewed: Ported: the 4.x getStackForBone/getTransformTypeForStack are GeckoLib 5's getRelevantBones (right_hand main hand, left_hand off hand, third-person contexts, stacks captured in addRenderData), and renderStackForBone is GeckoLib 5.3's submitItemStackRender override, which re-applies the bone pivot transform 5.3 no longer applies and then the same -90 degree X rotation and (1, 0, -3.75)/16 offset.

why: drops @Override from getStackForBone, getTransformTypeForStack and keeps the method: it then overrides nothing and never runs -- port it to the new signature, or delete it and say what vanilla now does instead
reviewed: (inherited from 1.21.5) Ported: GeckoLib 5 replaced getStackForBone/getTransformTypeForStack with getRelevantBones (RenderData per bone) and a renderStackForBone that takes the display context; both methods are now called from those overrides, reading the hand stacks captured in addRenderData, so the shield's NONE context still applies.

reviewed: Ported: render(state, pose, MultiBufferSource, light) is submit(state, pose, SubmitNodeCollector, camera) since 1.21.9; the override calls super and queues the death rays (progress and half height captured in extractRenderState) as custom geometry on RenderType.lightning(), the only type DeathRayLayer draws with, from the same pose.

(inherited from 1.21.4) The emptied bodies are the old BlockEntityWithoutLevelRenderer constructor's super(...) call (a special model renderer has no base to construct) and the record's trivial members; the render body is unchanged and is registered via RegisterSpecialModelRendererEvent and items/lightning_spear.json.
